sections.heading: Dudhsagar Dairy: The Mehsana District Milk Union
paragraphs: The Mehsana District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union, known as Dudhsagar Dairy, was incorporated in 1960 under Gujarat's Anand Pattern and sells under the Amul and Sagar brands. It began with an average collection of 3,300 litres a day from 11 village societies; its own figures for FY 2025-26 give average collection of 36.34 lakh litres a day and a turnover of about Rs 9,043 crore.
The union says it serves more than 4.70 lakh producers in over 1,153 villages of Mehsana, Patan and Gandhinagar districts, and more than 10 lakh farmer members across six states.

sections.heading: How the Mehsana Plant Grew
paragraphs: Dudhsagar's milestones record a first powder and pasteurisation plant of 90,000 litres in 1965, processing capacity raised to 4.5 lakh litres a day in 1979, a fourth milk powder plant in 1984 and a sweetened condensed milk plant in 1993. The union's highest single-day intake, 40.25 lakh litres, was recorded on 12 January 2018.
A line that has grown in stages like this usually carries tube of several ages and wall thicknesses, so replacement work starts with measuring what is already installed.

sections.heading: Kadi, Patan and the Plants Beyond Mehsana
paragraphs: ICRA's October 2022 rating report says Dudhsagar owns six dairy plants in and around Mehsana with a combined 33 lakh litres a day, plus plants at Manesar and Dharuhera in Haryana of 10 lakh litres a day each, for a total of 53 lakh litres a day on 31 March 2022. The same report noted a planned debt-funded modernisation and expansion of UHT capacity, expected to finish by FY2024.

Locally, the Kadi chilling centre was converted into Dudhvihasagar Dairy in 2013 and later added dahi manufacturing of 10,000 kg a day. The union lists the Mehsana, Patan, Kadi and Harij plants as ISO 22000:2018 and ISO 9001:2015 certified, and Vihar as FSSC 22000 certified.

sections.heading: Specifying Tube for Mehsana UHT, Dahi and Powder Lines
paragraphs: UHT product lines, dahi and buttermilk, condensed milk and the evaporator feed ahead of powder drying are where fouling and repeated CIP decide tube life, so we supply 316L to ASTM A270 with an SF4 electropolished bore there. Every electropolished lot comes with an Ra report and an EN 10204 3.1 certificate traced to the heat number.

Milk reception from village tankers, chilled water and cleaning-solution returns are normally fine in SF1 or mill-finish 304L, which lets a large Mehsana order put the higher finish only where the product touches the wall.

sections.heading: What to Send With a Mehsana Enquiry
bullets: Plant section: reception, pasteuriser, UHT, dahi and buttermilk, condensed milk, powder or CIP
Outside diameter, wall thickness and metres needed for each size
Grade and bore finish: 316L SF4, 304L SF1 or mill finish
Standard to meet: ASTM A270, A269 or ASME BPE, with any Ra limit
Fittings to quote with the tube: bends, tees, ferrules or reducers
Measurements or a drawing where new tube joins an existing run

sections.heading: Delivery to Mehsana and North Gujarat
paragraphs: Mehsana orders go by road from Mumbai, with every electropolished length capped and sleeved, and the dispatch date and transit are confirmed in writing when the order is placed. Each length is PMI-checked before it leaves, and a complete enquiry gets a quotation within 24 hours.
